name: Ekeby Manor and its Crofts
region: Östergötland, on the plain south of Lake Roxen
description: Ekeby is an old noble estate on the fertile Östergötland plain: a white manor house with two wings at the end of an avenue of limes, a home farm, its own mill, and some twenty tenant crofts scattered along the forest edge whose holders owe the estate days of labour. The present owner, a baron, spends the winters in Stockholm and has begun to replace the crofters with contract labourers (statare) paid in kind.
seasonNotes: April, the spring thaw. The snow has gone from the fields but lies grey in the forest; the roads are axle-deep in mud and almost impassable. Meltwater fills every ditch and the stream runs loud and brown over the mill weir. The first lapwings and larks return over the fields. Ploughing waits for the ground to dry; the crofters are spreading manure and mending fences. Easter falls this month.
travel: From Uppsala by rail via Stockholm and Katrineholm to Norrköping, about eight hours, then by the newest stretch of the eastern line or by coach, and the last miles in the estate's carriage on roads deep in thaw mud.
publicFacts: The baron's family has owned Ekeby since the 1600s; the present baron spends winters in Stockholm and is often away.
The estate's steward manages the farm and the crofts in the baron's absence and is not well liked.
Crofters at Ekeby owe three days of labour a week in summer and two in winter, with a horse.
The baron has begun replacing crofters with statare families living in a long barracks at the home farm.
Two crofts were pulled down last year when their tenants left for America.
Ekeby's mill grinds for the estate and for the parish farmers, who pay a toll in grain.
The parish church contains the burial vault of the baron's family.
Ekeby's library is said to be one of the finest in the province.

places.name: Ekeby Manor
places.description: The manor stands white and severe at the end of a lime avenue whose trees are still bare, with crows building in the tops. Meltwater gurgles in the gutters and the gravel forecourt is soft with mud. In the windows the shutters are still half closed against the winter. Inside, the house smells of wax polish, stove heat and old wood.

places.name: Ekeby Home Farm
places.description: The home farm stands behind the manor, a big quadrangle of red-painted barns, stables and cowsheds enclosing a muddy yard. The statare barracks is a long low building at one side, with children playing in the slush. Dung heaps steam in the cold morning. The steward's voice carries across the yard.

places.name: Lyckan Croft
places.description: Lyckan is a red croft on a rise at the forest edge, with a lilac bush beside the door still bare of leaves. The thaw has made a pond of the yard and planks are laid across it. A cow and a pig shift in the byre. The crofter's wife is boiling washing in a pot over a fire outside.

places.name: Kärret Croft
places.description: Kärret lies in a wet hollow by the forest, half its potato field under meltwater. The cottage is grey and needs a new roof, patched with birch bark. Smoke struggles out of the chimney in the damp air. A path leads into the forest, where the estate's woodcutters are working.

places.name: Ekeby Mill
places.description: The estate mill is a solid stone building on the stream below the manor, roaring with the spring flood. The weir is hidden under a curtain of brown water, and spray fogs the air. The miller has opened every sluice to spare the dam. Inside, the floor trembles with the wheel.

places.name: Ekeby Church
places.description: The parish church is a white medieval building on a mound in the fields, with the baron's family chapel built onto the north side. Snowdrops have come up in the churchyard among the old stones. Inside, the family's coats of arms hang on the walls. The bell rings for Easter with a sound that carries across the wet fields.

affordances.name: Bell tower
affordances.description: Steep ladders up to the bells, bird droppings on the beams, wind through the louvres.

affordances.name: Church loft

affordances.name: Burial vault
affordances.description: The baronial burial vault, its iron door bearing the family's arms, coffins stacked on shelves in the brick dark.

places.name: Ekeby Parsonage
places.description: The parsonage is a comfortable yellow house a short walk from the church, its garden bare and wet. The vicar is a scholar who corresponds with the university in Uppsala. Crows walk in the ploughed glebe land. Inside, a fire is lit in every room against the spring damp.

places.name: The Estate Smithy
places.description: The estate smithy stands by the road at the edge of the home farm, busy with ploughshares and harrow teeth for the coming spring work. Mud is trodden in and out of the open door. The smith is a crofter who pays his rent in iron work. The forge glow is warm in the grey April day.
